pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where should beginners stay in the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Wherever
   B. The deep end
   C. Under a diving board
   D. The shallow end

2. Floating means (1 mark)
   A. sinking
   B. diving
   C. swimming fast
   D. staying on top of the water without swimming

3. In water tag, players (1 mark)
   A. run on the pool side
   B. hold others under water
   C. walk fast, not run, and tag gently
   D. push others

4. Which float has the body curled up like a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Prone float
   B. Glide
   C. Supine float
   D. Mushroom float

5. What helps your body to float? (1 mark)
   A. Kicking hard only
   B. Holding a stone
   C. Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air
   D. Being heavy

6. How does the hawk tag? (1 mark)
   A. By pulling clothes
   B. By pushing
   C. By tripping
   D. Gently on the back or shoulders

7. How are indigenous games mostly learnt? (1 mark)
   A. By reading long books only
   B. By watching and joining in
   C. By watching TV only
   D. By buying kits

8. An elephant walk suits which rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. No beat
   B. A whistle
   C. Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   D. Very fast ta-te ta-te

9. The snake slither is done (1 mark)
   A. running fast
   B. hopping
   C. standing on tiptoe
   D. lying on the tummy and wriggling forward

10. Counting steps and jumps in animal games links to (1 mark)
   A. Chemistry
   B. Foreign languages only
   C. Mathematics
   D. Geography maps

11. Which Kiswahili word means frog? (1 mark)
   A. tembo
   B. kaa
   C. chura
   D. twiga

12. Animal games are inspired by (1 mark)
   A. cars
   B. the movements and behaviour of animals
   C. clouds
   D. tall buildings

13. In the giraffe stretch, you (1 mark)
   A. stand tall on toes with arms high
   B. roll
   C. crawl
   D. swim

14. Indigenous games are (1 mark)
   A. traditional games that belong to a people and place
   B. games from space
   C. games with no rules
   D. games played only with computers

15. Every displayed work should have (1 mark)
   A. no name
   B. a price only
   C. a label with the title and artist's name
   D. a secret code

16. The Kenya National Anthem is a (1 mark)
   A. a game
   B. a topical song about washing
   C. a work song
   D. national symbol

17. Which is an example of appropriate behaviour when viewing a display? (1 mark)
   A. Touching wet paint
   B. Laughing at others
   C. Being quiet and respectful
   D. Running

18. To appreciate a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. destroy it
   B. notice, understand and value it
   C. copy it exactly
   D. hide it

19. Verse 1 of the anthem asks (1 mark)
   A. for a holiday
   B. for a new school
   C. God to bless the nation
   D. for money

20. When presenting your artwork, you should hold it (1 mark)
   A. by one corner and shake
   B. by the middle with wet hands
   C. carefully by the edges
   D. upside down

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write rhythm patterns for the elephant walk and the hare hop using rhythm names. (3 marks)

22. Explain what is meant by two stars and a wish in feedback. (3 marks)

23. Explain how to perform an animal game to a musical rhythm. (4 marks)

24. Describe how to do the mushroom float. (3 marks)

25. Describe how to present an artwork from your portfolio. (4 marks)

26. How should you behave when the Kenya National Anthem is sung? (3 marks)

27. Why do we play water games in shallow water with the teacher? (3 marks)

28. Describe how to do the crab walk and name the muscles it strengthens. (3 marks)

29. Describe the steps of a glide. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The shallow end
   Shallow water is safer.

2. D — staying on top of the water without swimming
   Floating is resting on the surface.

3. C — walk fast, not run, and tag gently
   No pushing.

4. D — Mushroom float
   The tucked body with the back at the surface is the mushroom float.

5. C — Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air
   Buoyancy and air in the lungs.

6. D — Gently on the back or shoulders
   Gentle tagging keeps everyone safe.

7. B — By watching and joining in
   Elders and children play together.

8. C — Slow steady beats such as taa taa taa
   Slow heavy steps.

9. D — lying on the tummy and wriggling forward
   The body moves side to side like a snake.

10. C — Mathematics
   Counting is a maths skill.

11. C — chura
   Chura is a frog.

12. B — the movements and behaviour of animals
   Children copy how animals move.

13. A — stand tall on toes with arms high
   Reach up like a giraffe.

14. A — traditional games that belong to a people and place
   They are passed on by playing together.

15. C — a label with the title and artist's name
   Labels help viewers.

16. D — national symbol
   Like the flag, it stands for the nation.

17. C — Being quiet and respectful
   Respect for others' work is important.

18. B — notice, understand and value it
   Appreciation is valuing with understanding.

19. C — God to bless the nation
   The first verse is a prayer for blessing.

20. C — carefully by the edges
   Careful handling keeps it clean.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Elephant walk: taa taa taa (rest). Hare hop: ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern, 1 mark for correct rest or names.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say two good things about the work and then give one suggestion for improvement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a game and a rhythm, clap or drum the beat, move to the beat, change the speed for different animals and add a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: In shallow water take a breath and put the face in. Bend the knees and hug them to the chest with the chin tucked. The back rises to the surface. Hold for a few seconds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold it carefully, say the title, explain the materials and skills, tell the message, say what you like and what you would change, and listen to feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stand straight and still, face the flag, remove your cap, sing clearly and do not talk or play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: To feel safe and in control, to learn to breathe and move with confidence and to avoid accidents.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit, put hands behind, lift the hips and walk on hands and feet with tummy up. It strengthens the arms, shoulders and tummy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 1 mark for walking, 1 mark for muscles.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stand with the back to the wall and arms stretched overhead. Put the feet on the wall and bend the knees. Take a breath and put the face in. Push off gently with the body straight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
